likelyCauses: 1. ACCUMULATED DEPRECIATION ANOMALY: Balance sheet shows accumulated depreciation on Shop Assets increased by $48,543.23 ($160,065.84 - $111,522.61), but P&L reports only $14,853.55 in depreciation expense. The $33,689.68 excess may represent asset write-offs or disposals not fully captured in the investing section. If additional asset disposals occurred, proceeds may be unrecorded in the data provided.

2. INVESTMENT INCOME CLASSIFICATION: Northwestern Mutual account increased by $24,276.55 ($317,374.28 - $293,097.73). P&L reports $14,321.26 in investment income (4201). The $9,955.29 difference between the account growth and reported income may represent unrealized gains, reinvested dividends, or additional deposits not classified in the P&L. If Northwestern Mutual is an investment account rather than a cash equivalent, it should be reclassified to investing activities, which would significantly change the reconciliation.

3. MISSING TRANSACTION DATA: The General Ledger and Chart of Accounts were not provided. Transactions such as loan proceeds, member equity contributions, inter-account transfers, or other cash movements may exist that are not visible in the summary Balance Sheet and P&L alone.
4. WILDAPRICOT TIMING: One WildApricot payment of $250.00 dated 2025-08-05 (Testing, Scott) falls within the reporting period but may not be fully reconciled in QuickBooks.

5. UNEARNED REVENUE RECLASSIFICATION: The $27,783.50 decrease in Unearned Fundraising Revenue (2214) represents prior-year cash already received being recognized as revenue in 2025. This is correctly treated as a deduction in operating activities (cash was received in a prior period), but the magnitude of this item combined with the investment account growth creates the observed gap.
recommendedActions: Obtain QuickBooks General Ledger for 2025 to identify all cash transactions.
Clarify whether Northwestern Mutual Investment Services is a true cash equivalent or an investment account requiring separate investing activity classification.
Reconcile fixed asset sub-ledger to explain the $33,689.68 excess in accumulated depreciation change vs. P&L depreciation expense.
Confirm all asset disposal proceeds are recorded in QuickBooks.
Review inter-account transfers between bank accounts that may net to zero but affect individual account balances.

partI_summary.missionStatement: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild promotes the art and craft of woodworking through education, community, and shared access to tools and facilities. The Guild provides skills education, safety training, membership programs, and community events to advance woodworking knowledge among its members and the public.

partIII_programServiceAccomplishments.missionStatement: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild promotes the art and craft of woodworking through education, community, and shared access to tools and facilities. The Guild provides skills education, safety training, membership programs, and community events to advance woodworking knowledge among its members and the public.

programServices.description: MEMBERSHIP PROGRAM: The Guild provided member access to a fully equipped woodworking shop, tools, and facilities located at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO. Members received access to shop equipment, storage, library resources, and participation in Guild activities. Membership dues revenue of $171,525 supported ongoing operations and member services throughout 2025.

WOODWORKING SKILLS EDUCATION: The Guild offered structured woodworking skills education classes including Rough to Ready introductory courses, intermediate woodworking, bandsaw box, project finishing, hand tool woodworking, and other skill-building classes. Classes were taught by volunteer instructors and generated $50,217 in program revenue during 2025. Expenses included instructor materials, merchant fees, and related program costs.

SHOP FACILITIES AND OCCUPANCY: The Guild maintained and operated a dedicated woodworking shop facility under a lease agreement, providing members with access to a safe and well-equipped workspace. Rent expense of $150,000 represents the primary occupancy cost for the Guild's facility at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO. Rent income of $26,016 was received from sublease arrangements with affiliated organizations including KC Woodturners.

OTHER PROGRAM SERVICES: Includes woodworking safety education ($5,800 revenue; $2,902 expense), program events ($7,995 revenue; $12,567 expense), merchandise sales ($2,805 revenue; $4,841 expense), raffle ($2,548 revenue; $830 expense), storage income ($7,231 revenue), library income ($176 revenue; $96 expense), assets sold ($2,783 revenue; $2,783 expense), other program income ($5,267 revenue), gift-in-kind income ($4,590), sponsor income ($2,200), and related program software, newsletter, shop supplies, equipment, A/V, insurance, and depreciation expenses.

line4d_otherProgramServices.description: Other program services including safety education, program events, merchandise, raffle, storage, library, assets sold, other program income, gift-in-kind, and sponsor income with associated program expenses.

partI_publicCharityStatus.description: An organization that normally receives a substantial part of its support from a governmental unit or from the general public described in section 170(b)(1)(A)(vi). The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild is a publicly supported organization under IRC section 509(a)(1) and 170(b)(1)(A)(vi), receiving substantial support from membership dues, program service fees, and public contributions.

scheduleO.narrative: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild Inc is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization incorporated in Missouri in 1992. The Guild's mission is to promote the art and craft of woodworking through education, community, and shared access to tools and facilities. The Guild operates a fully equipped woodworking shop at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO 64108, providing members with access to professional-grade equipment, educational classes, safety training, special interest groups (SIGs), monthly membership meetings, and community events. The Guild offers structured programs including Rough to Ready introductory woodworking courses, intermediate and advanced skills classes, safety certification, project finishing, hand tool woodworking, CNC, laser engraving, carving, and other specialty programs. The Guild also hosts fundraising events and community outreach activities including the National Craft Open Studios Weekend. Membership is open to the public and the Guild serves woodworkers of all skill levels in the greater Kansas City metropolitan area.
